rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ohm's law is V = I R for a metal at constant temperature, and the I–V graph is then a straight line. A filament leaves that line as it heats, and a diode does not have one resistance at all. The law is used inside the range where R is constant.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The ohm is 1 V per ampere.  ·  A constantan wire is chosen in the laboratory because its resistance changes little with temperature.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Ohm's law says that the current in a metallic conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it, if the temperature and the physical state stay constant. The constant ratio V/I is the resistance.  ·  Plotted with current vertical and voltage horizontal, an ohmic resistor is a straight line through the origin. The slope is 1/R. A steeper line is a smaller resistance.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Proportionality needs constant temperature.  ·  The I–V graph of an ohmic metal is a straight line.  ·  A lamp curves as it heats.  ·  A diode conducts differently each way.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ohm's law: V = IR; R = ρL/A (resistivity ρ depends on material).  ·  Series: R = ΣR; same I, voltages add. Parallel: 1/R = Σ1/R; same V, currents add.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The law is a limited description. A filament lamp heats as the current rises, its resistance increases, and the graph bends. You cannot take one R from a cold measurement and use it at white heat.  ·  A semiconductor diode is non-ohmic in a stronger way. It conducts easily in forward bias and almost not at all in reverse bias. No single R describes it.  ·  A thermistor and an electrolyte can also leave the straight line. Quoting V = I R for them without a stated temperature and a stated operating point is not justified.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ ohm's law: v = ir; r = ρl/a (resistivity ρ depends on material)..  ·  Ohm's law is not a law of every component.  ·  The temperature condition is part of the statement.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Slope of I against V is 1/R.  ·  A diode has no single resistance.  ·  Write the constant-temperature condition.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Do not apply one R to a glowing lamp.  ·  Write V = I R at constant temperature and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R; internal resistance makes terminal V = E − Ir.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: ohm's law: v = ir; r = ρl/a (resistivity ρ depends on material).  ·  Inside the range where the metal stays ohmic, the law is still the working tool for series and parallel circuits. The limitation is the range, not a reason to abandon the law for a carbon resistor at a steady temperature.  ·  # Ohm's law and its limitations ## 1.
